checks: Inspect and re-grease the bearing; check for audible grinding.
Check shaft alignment and belt or coupling tension.
Compare vibration spectrum with a known-good reference if available.
hypotheses.summary: Mechanical friction appears first as vibration, then as heat, then as extra motor load.
hypotheses.title: Bearing wear / lubrication loss

checks: Inspect and clean the intake filter or strainer.
Check suction line for kinks, air leaks or a partly closed valve.
hypotheses.summary: Flow and pressure fall first, the motor unloads, then cavitation adds vibration and heat.
hypotheses.title: Clogged or restricted intake

checks: Check that the discharge valve is open and not stuck.
Inspect downstream piping and any filter for blockage.
Verify the pressure relief path works.
hypotheses.summary: Pressure spikes first, flow collapses, then load, vibration and heat rise.
hypotheses.title: Discharge blockage (closed or stuck valve)

checks: Measure supply voltage under load at the machine terminals.
Check the power supply, connectors and cable length or gauge.
Look for other loads that switch on at the same time.
hypotheses.summary: Voltage falls first, the motor compensates with more current, hydraulic output drops afterwards.
hypotheses.title: Supply voltage sag (brownout)

payload.narrative: The recorder triggered at T+00:06:24 on Vibration, which had sat 4.8 standard deviations from its learned baseline for several consecutive samples. Looking back through the buffer, the first channel to leave its baseline was Vibration (rising), 30 s before the trigger. It was followed by Bearing temperature (rising) 46 s later; Motor current (rising) 110 s later. The observed order best matches the known pattern 'Bearing wear / lubrication loss' (match score 1.00): Mechanical friction appears first as vibration, then as heat, then as extra motor load. Note: an onset order shows sequence, not proof of cause.
